# Niels Erik Nandal — Extended Site Guide

Canonical site: https://nielseriknandal.com/
Content index updated: 2026-07-20

## Profile

Niels Erik Nandal is an AI systems engineer building ambitious products with deterministic backends, legible interfaces, and readable software. His portfolio emphasizes Python, TypeScript, machine learning, backend correctness, explicit contracts, and product-focused engineering. He is open to full-time roles in AI and software engineering.

Canonical profile links:

- Website: https://nielseriknandal.com/
- GitHub: https://github.com/NielsdaWheelz
- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/nielseriknandal/
- X: https://x.com/the_powertool
- Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/nnandal

## Technical areas represented on the site

- Languages: Python, TypeScript, and SQL.
- Backend and data: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, SQLModel, Alembic, PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery, and Express.
- AI and machine learning: PyTorch, scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy, retrieval-augmented generation, LangGraph, and agent orchestration.
- Frontend: React, Next.js, TanStack Query, Tailwind CSS, and Vite.
- Engineering tools: Docker, Git, Linux, Bash, Make, and JSON-based interfaces.

These lists summarize the checked-in CV. The canonical CV is at https://nielseriknandal.com/cv.

## Projects

### Nexus

Canonical case study: https://nielseriknandal.com/projects/nexus
Repository: https://github.com/NielsdaWheelz/nexus-web
Live application: https://nexus.nielseriknandal.com

Nexus is a production reading, notes, and AI workspace for connected, inspectable knowledge work. It ingests books, papers, web articles, videos, podcasts, and browser captures into a shared resource model. The current system combines stable reader coordinates, highlights, a block-based notes outliner, hybrid search, durable branchable chat, citations represented as resource-graph edges, a multi-pane web workspace, an Android shell, and a browser extension. Its production topology uses a Next.js frontend and BFF, FastAPI services, PostgreSQL with pgvector, a Postgres-backed worker, and R2 object storage. The project began as a Fractal group project with Nyan and Jahnik; Niels subsequently rebuilt and independently develops the current `nexus-web` product.

### niels-gpt

Canonical case study: https://nielseriknandal.com/projects/niels-gpt
Repository: https://github.com/NielsdaWheelz/niels-gpt

niels-gpt is a small, end-to-end LLM system designed for a laptop or CPU. The project covers tokenizer training, dataset ingestion, token caches, decoder-only transformer training, supervised fine-tuning, checkpoint provenance, KV-cache prefill and decoding, benchmarking, and a chat interface. It deliberately favors explicit invariants and debuggability over a large framework stack.

### Factory Simulator

Canonical case study: https://nielseriknandal.com/projects/factory-simulator
Repository: https://github.com/NielsdaWheelz/factory-simulator

Factory Simulator combines LLM-based interpretation and briefing with a deterministic factory-scheduling and metrics core. The case study describes validated onboarding and decision pipelines, scenario generation, an earliest-due-date scheduler, reproducible metrics, Pydantic contracts, and traceable fallbacks.

### Suno Session Lab

Canonical case study: https://nielseriknandal.com/projects/suno-demo
Repository: https://github.com/NielsdaWheelz/suno-demo

Suno Session Lab turns clip generation into a branching, navigable space. It combines swappable music and embedding providers, clustering, generated cluster labels, lineage-aware UI, and centroid-guided "more like this" regeneration. The implementation is explicitly scoped as a demo without authentication or persistence.

### Fractal Chat

Canonical case study: https://nielseriknandal.com/projects/fractal-chat
Repository: https://github.com/NielsdaWheelz/fractal-chat

Fractal Chat is a chat-first reader for web pages, PDFs, and EPUBs. The case study covers extraction, crawling, chunking, embeddings, Postgres vector search, character-offset annotations, permissions, document-grounded chat, retrieval tools, and cross-document mentions.

### Fractal Go

Canonical case study: https://nielseriknandal.com/projects/fractal-go
Repository: https://github.com/NielsdaWheelz/fractal-go

Fractal Go is a real-time multiplayer Go application. Its case study focuses on WebSocket synchronization, capture detection, connected-group and liberty logic, ko prevention, territory scoring, and lessons from decomposing a first full-stack project.

## Writing

### Neural Networks from Zero: Embeddings and Backpropagation

Canonical article: https://nielseriknandal.com/writing/zero-to-hero-one
Published: 2025-11-18

A plain-English walkthrough of a small next-note network: learned embeddings, hidden layers, logits, cross-entropy, backpropagation, and autoregressive generation.

### Xavier, Kaiming, and Batch Normalization Explained

Canonical article: https://nielseriknandal.com/writing/zero-to-hero-two
Published: 2025-11-18

An explanation of activation scale, tanh saturation, dead ReLUs, when Xavier and Kaiming initialization apply, and how batch normalization behaves during training and inference.

### Building My First Real-Time Full-Stack App

Canonical article: https://nielseriknandal.com/writing/my-first-project
Published: 2025-09-27

A reflection on building a real-time multiplayer Go application, decomposing unfamiliar game logic, synchronizing state, and designing before styling.
